title: The 7-Step System Design Framework
description: Master the repeatable 7-step framework used by top engineers to tackle any system design interview question.

data.text: System design interviews can feel overwhelming because they are open-ended. A strong framework gives you a repeatable structure so you spend your energy designing, not figuring out what to do next. The 7-step framework used in this course breaks the problem into manageable phases: understanding the problem, defining requirements, estimating scale, designing the core components, addressing bottlenecks, and discussing trade-offs.

terms.definition: A repeatable process or set of steps used to solve a class of problems.
A compromise between two desirable but competing design goals, such as latency versus consistency.

blocks.text: The Seven Steps at a Glance

rows: Clear problem statement and user goals
Caching, load balancing, and partitioning plan
Comparison of alternatives and their costs
Detailed design for the most interesting component

data.caption: High-level flow of the 7-step system design framework.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Understand Problem] --> B[Define Requirements]
    B --> C[Estimate Scale]
    C --> D[Design Core Components]
    D --> E[Address Bottlenecks]
    E --> F[Discuss Trade-offs]
    F --> G[Deep Dive One Area]
    G --> H[Complete Design]

data.title: Use This Every Time
data.text: Even for simpler problems, walk through all seven steps out loud. Interviewers care about your process as much as your final answer.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The 7-step framework converts an open-ended question into a structured conversation.
Start with requirements before drawing any boxes.
Scale estimates come before component design.
Trade-offs show maturity; always discuss at least one alternative.
data.takeaway: A repeatable framework reduces cognitive load and lets you showcase engineering judgment.

items.question: Can I skip steps if the question seems simple?
items.answer: No. Briefly restating requirements and scale shows rigor and gives the interviewer a chance to correct your assumptions.

items.question: How much time should I spend on each step?
items.answer: Requirements and scale together should take about five to ten minutes. The remaining steps share the rest of the interview time.
